h1: Fence Painting and Staining in Alachua, FL
heroIntro: Privacy fences in subdivisions, picket fences near Main Street, and long property-line runs on the north end of town, cleaned, repaired, and stained or painted.

questions: Should I stain or paint my wood fence in Alachua?
Can a gray, sun-damaged fence be restored?
How long does fence staining take on a large lot?

body: Fences in Alachua come in all sizes. There's the six-foot privacy fence behind a home in Savannah Station, a short picket fence on an older lot near Main Street, and hundreds of feet of board fencing along a large lot on the north end. Every one of them faces the same sun, and the south-facing side usually turns gray and splintered first. Fence painting in Alachua, FL is mostly about stopping that damage before boards start to split and cup.
We wrote a local guide on this exact problem: how to treat a sun-damaged wood fence in Alachua. It's worth reading before deciding whether to stain or paint.

On most wood fences we recommend a penetrating stain. It soaks into the wood instead of forming a film, so there's nothing to peel when moisture moves through the boards. Paint makes sense if a fence was painted before or has to match painted trim on the house, but it needs more upkeep once it starts to break down. Vinyl fences usually need cleaning more than coating, and we'll tell you if that's all yours needs.

bullets: Washing to remove gray fibers, mildew, and old failing stain
Light sanding where boards have gone fuzzy or splintered
Replacing broken pickets or rails, each listed on the estimate first
Spraying and back-brushing so stain gets into the gaps and end grain
Protecting landscaping, driveways, and the neighbor's side as needed

body: On large lots, footage drives the schedule. A long property-line fence may take several days of washing, drying, and staining, and we'll lay out that schedule in writing. Fall through spring is the easiest time because wood dries faster between steps. Summer jobs are planned for mornings. If the fence meets a deck, staining both at once with Alachua deck staining keeps the color consistent. For a quick cleanup, start with pressure washing. More detail on products is on our Florida deck and fence staining page, and the Alachua page lists every service in town.

faqs.q: Can a gray, weathered fence be brought back?
faqs.a: Usually. Washing and light sanding remove the damaged surface fibers. As long as the boards are still solid, a penetrating stain will protect them again. Badly split or rotted boards are replaced.

faqs.q: Can you match the fence stain to my deck?
faqs.a: Yes. If both are being done, we use the same stain product and color so they read as one finish. If the deck was stained earlier, we can match it from a sample board or the leftover can.

faqs.q: Do you stain both sides of the fence?
faqs.a: If you have access to both sides, yes. On a shared fence we can do just your side, and the estimate will say which sides are included.

faqs.q: Is stain or paint better for a Florida wood fence?
faqs.a: For most wood fences, penetrating stain holds up better because it doesn't form a film that peels. Paint works when it needs to match the house trim or the fence was already painted.
